strengths: Rigorous theoretical framework: Propositions 1-2 formally establish hard constraint preservation (symplecticity and projection properties by construction) with elegant proofs
Novel architecture: Cotangent-lifted constrained autoencoder combined with geometric HNN is creative and well-motivated; hard constraints preferable to soft penalties
Comprehensive experimental validation: Systematic ablations isolating contributions of AE architecture, latent HNN design, and integrator choice across three systems with appropriate baselines
Geometric rigor: Proper application of Riemannian geometry to SPD manifolds (mass-inertia, damping matrices) with consistent empirical improvements over Cholesky-based approaches
Significant practical extension: Extends HNNs from 2-5 DoF to 600 DoF; handles conservative, dissipative, and non-separable Hamiltonians
Strong reproducibility: Detailed appendices (A-H) with architecture specifications, dataset generation, hyperparameters, and architecture choices enable reproduction
Clear presentation: Well-organized paper with effective use of figures (especially Fig. 1); mathematical exposition rigorous with appropriate background material
weaknesses: Fundamental scope limitation: Restricted to canonical symplectic forms (acknowledged but limits applicability); non-canonical systems excluded, severely constraining future impact

Questionable experimental claims: Table 2 reports 0.0 ± 0.0 symplecticity error for proposed method—numerical round-off should produce non-zero error. Either metric is inappropriate or claims require clarification
Baseline fairness concerns: 15-DoF HNN baseline 'was difficult to train' (p.7); unclear if equal hyperparameter tuning effort invested. Comparison may not be equitable
Ad hoc latent dimension selection: No principled method for choosing d; particle vortex shows d=6 outperforms d=10, but no clear guidance for practitioners; requires cross-validation
Modest generalization analysis: Tests show only 5-20× extension beyond training horizon; no systematic study of prediction error growth rates; limited evidence of true extrapolation

Limited dimensional scaling: 600 DoF modest by modern standards; computational benefits unclear (RO-HNN 26.34ms vs black-box HNN 8.04ms despite dimensionality reduction); claimed speedups not demonstrated
Narrow experimental scope: Only 3 simulated systems; pendulum is nearly 3-DoF; particle vortex unusual (no kinetic-potential separation); no real-world data or systems with model mismatch

Missing reproducibility details: No code/data release plan; datasets must be regenerated; hyperparameter sensitivity not analyzed (loss scaling λ varies 10³-10⁴); w (Strang integrator parameter) initialization unclear
Incomplete failure analysis: No discussion of failure modes; unclear when method breaks; robustness to noise unexplored; assumes system is well-reducible without verification
Limited scope of comparisons: No comparison to recent physics-informed methods (neural operators, graph neural networks for mechanics post-2024) or intrusive structure-preserving MOR baselines
